chapters.title: Menu items
chapters.subtitle: Links, content items, HTML and permissions

steps.text: A menu is a list of menu items, and the Menu module provides three types of them. In this video, we add a link, a content item, and an HTML item to a menu, and choose who sees an item.
A Link Menu Item links to an address you type. A Content Menu Item links to a content item you pick. An Html Menu Item links to an address, and shows HTML as the text of the link.
Link and Html items have a Permissions field. People who do not have the permissions you choose do not see the item.
A Content Menu Item has the option Check content permissions instead. It hides the item from people who may not view the content item it points to.
The HTML of an Html Menu Item is cleaned when the menu is displayed, to prevent custom scripts. The Sanitize Html setting controls this, and it is on by default.
Under Content, Menus, open the Main Menu. A separate video covers creating menus and arranging their items. Here, the Add Menu Item button adds an item to this one.
The Available Menu Items window lists the three types: Link Menu Item, Content Menu Item and Html Menu Item. Each one has its own Add button.
Let's add a Link Menu Item. It has a Name, which is the text of the link, and a Url that says where it leads. We name it Editor Guide, and link it to the documentation.
Target says where the link opens. It suggests values, and one of them opens the linked document in another window or tab, so the site stays open.
Publish adds the item to the menu. The menu editor lists it with its name and its address.

chapters.title: Content Menu Item
chapters.subtitle: A link to a content item

steps.text: Add Menu Item opens the same window. This time we choose Content Menu Item, which links to a content item of the site.
Name is the text of the link, so we type Hours. In Selected Content Item, we type to search, and pick the Opening Hours article.
No address is typed here. The link is built from the content item itself, so it leads to the address of that item.
Check content permissions stays off for a public page. Turn it on for restricted content, and cache the menu, as its hint advises. Then Publish adds the item.

chapters.title: Html Menu Item
chapters.subtitle: HTML as the text of the link

steps.text: The third type, the Html Menu Item, has the same Name, Url and Target fields as a link, and one more field for the HTML.
Let's name it Contact us, and link it to an email address, so that selecting it opens the email program of the visitor.
The Html field replaces the name as the text of the link, and sits inside the link. Let's make the first word italic.
The HTML is cleaned when the menu is displayed, because Sanitize Html is on by default. Publish adds the item to the menu.
To restrict an item, choose Edit on its row. Let's restrict Editor Guide, because it is meant for the people who work in the admin.
In Permissions, we type to search, and select Access admin panel. Only people who have this permission see the item. When you choose several, a person needs all of them.
A restricted item hides the items under it as well. Publish adds the change to the menu.
Each change is saved in a draft of the menu, so the site keeps showing the published menu until the menu itself is published.
Let's publish the Main Menu with the Publish button. A message confirms that your Menu has been published, and the editor stays on the menu.
On the site, signed in as the administrator, the menu lists Home, About, Editor Guide, Hours and Contact us, with the first word in italics.
A visitor who is not signed in gets the same menu without Editor Guide. The other items have no permissions, so everyone sees them.
That is how Link, Content and Html menu items work, and how permissions decide who sees them. A separate video covers how themes render menus. Thanks for watching.
